fieldValues.title: check-rfc-integration.mjs's manifest-token resolver had no concept:/mechanism: kind, so a subsection retirement could silently break an unrelated RFC's provenance citation
fieldValues.summary: The RFC integration manifest token grammar only recognized section:<slug>/subsection:<slug>, indexed solely from live com.semanticops.spec/section and /subsection records. Deleting a subsection whose content had moved into a concept or mechanism (the RFC-042 Change B destination Types) broke any RFC's manifest token that still cited it by its old slug, with no path to re-point the token at its actual new home.
evidence: srs#710 batch (PR #747, 2026-09-11): deleting the 'Version semantics' subsection (8e3fb02c) broke RFC-030's `subsection:version-semantics` token — check-rfc-integration.mjs failed with 'manifest token "subsection:version-semantics" does not resolve to any canonical record/schema' even though the content was verbatim preserved in the mechanism b3c293f9 ('Notational conventions')
scripts/check-rfc-integration.mjs (pre-fix): resolveToken() had cases for I-<n>, ext:, schema:, type:, section:, subsection:, cell: — no concept: or mechanism:

buildResolvers()'s switch(record.typeId) only populated sectionSlugs/subsectionSlugs from SECTION_TYPE/SUBSECTION_TYPE records — CONCEPT_TYPE (2a000004-...-000004) and MECHANISM_TYPE (6655e3fb-...) were not indexed at all before this fix
50 subsection records remain under srs#710 as of this finding; any of them could be cited by an RFC's manifest token the same way RFC-030 cited Version semantics
fieldValues.body:
## Fix applied

Added `CONCEPT_TYPE`/`MECHANISM_TYPE` constants, `conceptSlugs`/`mechanismSlugs` index sets populated the same way `sectionSlugs`/`subsectionSlugs` already were, and `concept:<slug>`/`mechanism:<slug>` cases in `resolveToken()` mirroring `section:`/`subsection:` exactly (same `slugify()`, same Set.has lookup). Documented the two new token kinds in `CLAUDE.md`'s integration-manifest section. Updated RFC-030's own manifest token from `subsection:version-semantics` to `mechanism:notational-conventions`.

Proved the fix is a real resolver, not an accidental pass-through: temporarily pointed RFC-030's token at `mechanism:does-not-exist-anywhere`, re-ran the checker, confirmed it failed with the expected message naming that exact token, then reverted to the correct value and confirmed green.

## Why this wasn't caught earlier

Earlier batches (#561-564, #744, #745) either didn't retire a subsection any RFC cited by title, or (per #744/#745's own reports) the retiring subsection's content moved into a *concept* the checker still couldn't resolve either — this class of failure needed a subsection with a live RFC citation to actually retire before it would surface. It's plausible other, not-yet-retired subsections are cited the same way and will hit this exact failure again unless the next worker checks proactively (see the companion carried_context record).

## Generalization

This is a durable capability, not a one-off patch for RFC-030: any future RFC (or Wave-2 finding) that needs to cite a concept or mechanism directly in its integration manifest can now do so with `concept:<slug>`/`mechanism:<slug>`, independent of whether that citation arose from a section/subsection retirement.
